thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: PD Alert #INC-20260315-7890 — high rate of TLS handshake failures from edge (eu-west-1). Auto-page to oncall.

pagerduty: Incident auto-created and paged: severity=high, symptom=TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAIL, affected=% of requests ~12-18%, affected region=EU-WEST.

Aisha Park: acked. I'm oncall — looking now. Any stack traces or recent deploys? :eyes:

Ben Chen: saw a cert rotation attempt 10m ago for edge-cert-2026-03 that targeted the new wildcard. Deployment log shows partial success across regions due to staging job hitting rate limits.

Priya S: customer-facing: a small subset of customers in EU complaining about 502 / TLS errors. We've got three active support threads. Marking impacted product: hosted-api.

ops-oncall: Observed ALB target health flapping around same time. Targets in eu-west behind autoscaler hitting 0/3 healthy intermittently. Could be healthcheck path timing out after cert change.

Aisha Park: ok — running quick checks. Can someone curl the edge from an EU probe?

Ben Chen: running remote curl from eu probe:

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.ai/health
*   Trying 13.32.50.121...
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (13.32.50.121) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake failure: alert handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'api.redwood.ai'
```

Ben Chen: error shows cert presented doesn't match host (CN mismatch) on some frontends. But other frontends show the new cert OK. Looks like partial cert rollout to edge proxies.

Aisha Park: that matches the timeframe. Any DNS changes?

network-team: DNS records for api.redwood.ai were updated earlier to add a new alias to edge-legacy while we roll certs. TTL was 300s but the change didn't propagate uniformly due to upstream caching.

Eugene M: TL;DR: two factors: partial cert rotation + DNS split where some clients hit newly-weighted hosts with the old cert. Combined causes handshake failures and ALB target health probes failing (because probe verifies TLS and gets different cert).

Priya S: customer impact estimate: ~12-18% of traffic in EU, mostly latency-sensitive API calls. No data exfil/compromise. Start external comms?

Aisha Park: hold on external comms until mitigation in place. Mitigation plan: 1) rollback cert rotation to previous cert on edge proxies (fast), 2) adjust LB traffic weight to shift EU traffic away from partial nodes -> edge-legacy pool, 3) reduce DNS TTL to 60 to speed subsequent changes if needed, 4) monitor healthchecks and client error rate.

ops-oncall: I can flip route weights. Doing weight shift now to send 90% traffic to edge-legacy for eu-west.

incident-bot: Action triggered: route-weight-change job started by ops-oncall.

Ben Chen: rolling back certs now on the subset of proxies that failed. Patch command:

```
# on edge-proxy cluster nodes with failing cert
sudo cp /etc/edge/certs/prev/wildcard.pem /etc/edge/certs/active.pem && sudo systemctl reload edge-proxy
```

Ben Chen: rollback issued to 8 nodes (eu-west). Reload succeeded on 7/8, one node returned timeout; marking for restart.

ops-oncall: route weight flip completed. Verifying metrics...

pagerduty: Aisha Park acknowledged incident at 2026-03-15T09:12:07Z.

Priya S: I'm seeing errors drop from 18% -> 4% within 45s of weight change. Support threads: customers report degraded -> mostly recovered.

Eugene M: healthchecks are stabilizing. The remaining failing proxy node shows disk pressure; I'm kicking a restart for it.

ops-oncall: restarted node, healthcheck passed.

Ben Chen: cert rollback confirmed across eu-west. ALB target health now 3/3 on all pools.

Aisha Park: good. Next steps: keep traffic on edge-legacy for 10m, then test blue-green rollout with smaller batch and stricter pre-checks. Also open a PR to tighten our cert-rotation job to guard against partial rollouts.

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation: auto-escalate to SRE Lead if ack not followed by resolution within 15m. (ack now present — escalation suppressed)

pagerduty: Incident updated: severity downgraded to medium. Incident status: mitigation in progress.

Priya S: starting customer comms draft: "We experienced a partial TLS certificate rotation affecting EU customers; traffic has been routed away and service restored. A post-incident update will follow." Sending to legal/comm for signoff.

Aisha Park: handing off to Ben and Eugene for root cause/next steps. I'm paged out after 15:30 local. Please keep me looped. @Ben Chen @Eugene M — you own runnable RCA and follow-up.

Ben Chen: taking RCA. First pass: cert-rotation job didn't wait for confirmation on rollout per-proxy and retried with partial success; combined with DNS alias add led to inconsistent fronting hosts. Will prepare timeline and PR.

Eugene M: I'll open a ticket with our CDN partner — some edge nodes had stale cert cache causing mismatch during live swap.

incident-bot: Note: On-call handoff scheduled to night shift in 4 hours. Current assignees: Ben Chen, Eugene M.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by Ben Chen at 2026-03-15T09:16:30Z. Escalation suppressed.

Priya S: closing loop: support threads updated, monitoring set, external comms queued.

Aisha Park: closing incident channel (we'll convert this to a postmortem thread). Thanks all. :clap:

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:20:45Z. Auto-create postmortem=YES, owner=Ben Chen.

Ben Chen: will publish a short postmortem by EOD with timeline, root cause, and action items: tighter cert rollout gate, DNS change checklist, and CDN cache invalidation step.

Eugene M: also adding follow-up: add unit to our chaos tests — simulate partial cert rotations + DNS weight shifts.

ops-oncall: leaving note: if any recurring TLS spikes appear, immediate rollback + traffic shift procedure is in the runbook under /runbooks/tls-cert-rotation.

Priya S: closing support alerts. Marking customers notified.

Aisha Park: final — incident closed.
